topics.title: Vector Equations of Circles, Spheres and Planes

questions.stem: The spheres \(S_1:x^2-2x+y^2+4y+z^2-4z=0\) and \(S_2:x^2+y^2+z^2+10x+2z+10=0\) intersect at exactly one point. Why?
questions.hint: Complete the squares to find the centres and radii, then compare distance with the sum of radii.
questions.solution: They are externally tangent: centre distance 7 equals radius sum 7.

steps.explain: Complete squares for S1.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100%" viewBox="0 0 480 250"><circle cx="155" cy="125" r="65" fill="#dbeafe" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="265" cy="125" r="65" fill="#fee2e2" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="210" cy="125" r="4" fill="#111827"/><text x="125" y="120">S₁</text><text x="270" y="120">S₂</text><text x="185" y="215">external tangency</text></svg>

steps.explain: Complete squares for S2.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100%" viewBox="0 0 480 250"><circle cx="155" cy="125" r="65" fill="#dbeafe" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="265" cy="125" r="65" fill="#fee2e2" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="210" cy="125" r="4" fill="#111827"/><text x="125" y="120">S₁</text><text x="270" y="120">S₂</text><text x="185" y="215">external tangency</text></svg>

steps.explain: Compare the centre distance and radii.
steps.work: Distance \(=\sqrt{6^2+(-2)^2+3^2}=7=3+4\); the spheres are externally tangent.

figure.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100%" viewBox="0 0 480 250"><circle cx="155" cy="125" r="65" fill="#dbeafe" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="265" cy="125" r="65" fill="#fee2e2" fill-opacity=".45" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="210" cy="125" r="4" fill="#111827"/><text x="125" y="120">S₁</text><text x="270" y="120">S₂</text><text x="185" y="215">external tangency</text></svg>

options: Their centre distance equals the sum of their radii.
Their centres coincide and their radii are equal.

questions.hint: Set \(|P-Q|^2=|P-R|^2\). Expand and cancel the matching \(x^2+y^2+z^2\) terms.
